title: 全球最高瀑布
source_line: 数据：世界瀑布数据库、吉尼斯世界纪录、秘鲁国家地理研究所（IGN）、美国地质调查局（USGS）

items.name: 安赫尔瀑布
items.subtitle: 卡奈依马国家公园

source.name: Guinness World Records: Tallest waterfall (1949 survey, 979 m)

cross_check.name: World Waterfall Database (counts only the 807 m main plunge)

items.notes: 979 m = 1949 survey of an expedition funded by National Geographic (Ruth Robertson), recognised by Guinness. WWD argues the survey was sighted from the Río Carrao/Caroní ~2 km away and includes ~170 m of river below the falls; it lists only the 807 m main plunge (−17.6%, >10%: kept 979 by our 'published survey/record first' rule — user to confirm). Guinness itself notes that if only 807 m counts, Tugela (948 m) is the tallest. Wikipedia list: 979 m.
items.image_hint: Angel Falls / Salto Ángel (Kerepakupai Merú), Auyán-tepui, Canaima National Park, Bolívar, Venezuela: ONE ultra-tall white ribbon free-falling from the flat-topped sandstone tepui wall into green jungle, mist at the base; classic full-height view from Mirador Laime / Ratoncito island or from a plane, rainy-season flow. NOT Kaieteur Falls (Guyana, wide river fall), NOT Kukenán or Roraima tepui falls, NOT Iguazú.

items.name: 图盖拉瀑布
items.subtitle: 德拉肯斯山脉

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Tugela Falls (total height 948 m); same figure in Guinness World Records

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD flow consistency 4 months (rainy season, Nov–Mar); WWD status 'Unconfirmed' but the 948 m figure is the one Guinness quotes, so it passes our 'independent record' rule. 2016 Czech team (Petr Jan Juračka) measured 983 m, but WWD says from >1 km below the falls; not used. Lower tiers hidden in a gorge; true height not settled.
items.image_hint: Tugela Falls, the Amphitheatre escarpment, Royal Natal National Park (Maloti-Drakensberg), KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa: thin white multi-tier ribbon leaping off the huge basalt Amphitheatre cliff, summer (green grass, flowing water); full-height view from the Tugela Gorge trail / valley looking up at the Amphitheatre, or from the top near the chain ladders. NOT frozen winter ice shots, NOT Howick Falls, NOT Maletsunyane Falls (Lesotho).

items.name: 马滕巴赫瀑布
items.subtitle: 劳特布龙嫩

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Mattenbachfälle (total height 930 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: Earlier estimate 840 m (still in Wikipedia list, −9.7%). In 2020 the Vertical Water Canyoning Team abseiled the falls and measured ~930 m (WWD), making it the tallest in Eurasia. Tiny 0.9 km² catchment — can dry out in late-summer drought, so no SEASONAL badge (WWD gives no flow-months figure).
items.image_hint: Mattenbachfälle (Mattenbach falls), on the EAST wall of the Lauterbrunnen Valley near Stechelberg, Bernese Oberland, Switzerland: a very tall, thin, multi-tier white stream sliding down the sheer limestone valley wall above green meadows; full height of the wall visible, ideally early summer snowmelt. NOT Staubbach Falls (village of Lauterbrunnen, single plunge by the church), NOT Mürrenbach Falls (west wall), NOT Trümmelbach Falls (inside the mountain).

items.name: 云比拉瀑布
items.subtitle: 亚马孙大区奎斯佩斯

source.name: Instituto Geográfico Nacional (Peru) laser survey 2007, 895.4 m (reported by MercoPress 2007-12-04; WWD)

cross_check.name: World Waterfall Database: Yumbilla (896 m)

items.notes: IGN Peru laser survey 2007: 895.4 m (displayed 895 m). WWD 896 m, Wikipedia list 896 m. WWD status Unconfirmed, admitted under our independent-survey rule. Flow regime not documented (best in rainy season); no badge.
items.image_hint: Yumbilla waterfall (Catarata de Yumbilla), near Cuispes, Bongará province, Amazonas region, northern Peru (Chachapoyas area): a very tall chain of thin white falls down a sheer cliff in dense green cloud forest; full-height view from the Cuispes trail. NOT Gocta waterfall (two big tiers, Cocachimba), NOT Chinata or Pabellón falls.

items.name: 斯科尔加瀑布
items.subtitle: 孙达尔

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Skorga (total height 875 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: Height from 1-m contour maps (WWD, visited/catalogued). Only the lower ~600 m is visible from the valley floor. WWD flow consistency 9 months (best April–July).
items.image_hint: Skorga waterfall (also spelled Skorgafossen / Skorgefossen), Sunndalen valley just east of Sunndalsøra, Sunndal, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: a long white horsetail stream down the steep valley wall beside Vinnufossen; early-summer snowmelt flow; view from the valley floor road (Rv70). NOT Vinnufossen (the broader neighbour), NOT Skorga in Tafjord if different.

items.name: 维努瀑布
items.subtitle: 孙达尔

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Vinnu (total height 845 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD (2026-10-13) says the recognised name is Vinnu (Vinnufallet) and calls Vinnufossen incorrect; kept the widely used name Vinnufossen on screen. Earlier WWD estimate 865 m, revised to 845 m. Glacier-fed; flow consistency 9 months (best May–Sept).
items.image_hint: Vinnufossen (Vinnufallet), above Sunndalsøra, Sunndal, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: fed by the Vinnu glacier, it shoots out of a crevice at the top of the valley wall then fans out into a wide white veil (150 m broad) down the mountainside; summer view from the Rv70 road / Sunndalsøra. NOT Skorga (neighbouring thinner fall).

items.name: 詹姆斯·布鲁斯瀑布
items.subtitle: 路易莎公主湾

source.name: World Waterfall Database: James Bruce Falls (total height 840 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: tallest fall it has catalogued in North America; small glacial source likely sustains year-round flow, but volume is low. No flow-months figure; no badge.
items.image_hint: James Bruce Falls, head of Princess Louisa Inlet (Jervis Inlet), British Columbia, Canada: a very tall, thin white thread high on the granite cliffs above the inlet, partly in a crevice; view from a boat on Princess Louisa Inlet or the Loquilts Creek trail. NOT Chatterbox Falls (the famous wide lower fall at the inlet's head).

items.name: 布朗瀑布
items.subtitle: 峡湾地区神奇峡湾

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Browne Falls (total height 836 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: falls drop out of Lake Browne at 836 m straight to Doubtful Sound; Te Ara and older sources give 619 m (2,031 ft) (−26%, >10%: WWD figure kept, it follows the topographic lake level). Year-round flow (WWD high-volume months 12).
items.image_hint: Browne Falls, above Hall Arm, Doubtful Sound (Patea), Fiordland National Park, New Zealand: steep white tiered cascades zig-zagging down a rainforest-covered fiord wall straight into the dark sea; view from a Doubtful Sound cruise boat. NOT Helena Falls (Deep Cove), NOT Milford Sound's Stirling or Bowen Falls.

items.name: 谢尔斯克雷德瀑布
items.subtitle: 韦斯特兰郡

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Kjerrskredfossen (total height 831 m)

items.notes: Two side-by-side streams; surveyed by WWD in 2011. Not in the Wikipedia list (no second source). Flow consistency 7 months (best March–June).
items.image_hint: Kjerrskredfossen, Nærøydalen valley just southwest of Gudvangen, Aurland, Vestland, Norway: two parallel white streams plunging and veiling in many tiers down the sheer 800 m cliffs of the Nærøy valley; spring snowmelt; view from the E16 / valley floor near Gudvangen. NOT Kjelfossen (the famous one right above Gudvangen at the fjord end), NOT Stalheimsfossen or Sivlefossen.

items.name: 怀希劳瀑布
items.subtitle: 夏威夷怀马努谷

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Waihilau Falls (total height 792 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: Height = amphitheatre wall per USGS topo (WWD). Flow consistency 12 months.
items.image_hint: Waihilau Falls, headwall of the remote Waimanu Valley, Kohala coast, Hawaiʻi Island (Big Island), USA: three impossibly tall, slender white threads veiling down a vertical cliff covered in lush green vegetation; helicopter / aerial or valley-floor view. NOT Hiʻilawe Falls (Waipiʻo Valley), NOT Akaka Falls.

items.name: 殖民地溪瀑布
items.subtitle: 北喀斯喀特山脉
items.image_credit: Northwest Waterfall Survey / All rights reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Colonial Creek Falls (total height 783 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD triangulated 783 m in Aug 2011 (earlier topo estimate 788 m, still in Wikipedia list; Wikipedia article 783 m). Flows all year (WWD).
items.image_hint: Colonial Creek Falls, North Cascades National Park, Washington, USA: a long chain of 13 white cascades and plunges from the Colonial Glacier down a dark rock headwall above Diablo Lake's Thunder Arm, among glaciated peaks; view from the Colonial/Pyramid Peak area or aerial. NOT Diablo Lake alone, NOT Gorge Creek Falls or Ladder Creek Falls.

items.name: 戈克塔瀑布
items.subtitle: 亚马孙大区科卡钦巴

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Gocta (total height 771 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: Measured 771 m (±13 m) by a survey organised by Stefan Ziemendorff and the Peruvian government, announced 2006; known to locals for centuries but not to the outside world. Perennial (Wikipedia; WWD 12 months).
items.image_hint: Gocta waterfall (Catarata de Gocta), near Cocachimba / San Pablo, Bongará, Amazonas, Peru (Chachapoyas): two big white plunges, a smaller upper tier and a huge 540 m lower plunge, from a sheer cliff in green cloud-forest mountains; full two-tier view from the Cocachimba trail. NOT Yumbilla (thinner multi-tier), NOT Chinata.

items.name: 谢尔瀑布
items.subtitle: 韦斯特兰郡居德旺恩

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Kjelfossen (total height 765 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD re-evaluated several times; current 765 m is for the centre stream (Vetle Kjelfossen). Wikipedia list 755 m (−1.3%). Flow consistency 10 months (best March–July).
items.image_hint: Kjelfossen, above the village of Gudvangen at the head of the Nærøyfjord, Aurland, Vestland, Norway: two or three parallel white streams dropping in many tiers down a towering cliff behind Gudvangen; view from Gudvangen village / the fjord. NOT Kjerrskredfossen (southwest in the valley), NOT Stalheimsfossen.

items.name: 伊塞拉瀑布
items.subtitle: 华盛顿州

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Isella Falls (total height 762 m)

items.notes: WWD estimate from topographic data: top tentatively at 6,650 ft, total ~762 m; could be taller. No second source. Glacier-fed; flow months not documented; no badge.
items.image_hint: Isella Falls, on the south face of Bonanza Peak above Railroad Creek near Holden Village, Glacier Peak Wilderness, Lake Chelan area, Washington, USA: many braided white meltwater streams sliding down the mountain from the Isella Glacier, merging into one; view from the Railroad Creek Trail. NOT Holden Lake, NOT Rainbow Falls (Stehekin).

items.name: 约翰内斯堡瀑布
items.subtitle: 北喀斯喀特山脉

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Johannesburg Falls (total height 751 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD from USGS topo: just over 2,400 ft from the glacier, ending in a ~800 ft drop. Flow months not documented; no badge.
items.image_hint: Johannesburg Falls, on Johannesburg Mountain opposite the Cascade Pass trailhead, North Cascades National Park, Washington, USA: a white glacier-fed stream falling down the steep north face of Johannesburg Mountain, under hanging glaciers; classic view from the Cascade Pass parking lot. NOT Cascade Pass meadows only.

items.name: 肖塔瀑布
items.subtitle: 韦斯特兰郡

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Tjøtafossen (total height 750 m)

items.notes: WWD: ~750 m from the glacier toe; top shifts as the glacier advances/retreats. Flow consistency 9 months. No second source.
items.image_hint: Tjøtafossen, Oldedalen valley next to the Briksdal glacier, Stryn, Vestland, Norway: meltwater from Tjøtabreen zig-zags down a smooth granite wall, then spreads into a broad white veil over barren ground; summer view. NOT Briksdalsbreen glacier tongue itself, NOT Volefossen (by the Briksdal road).

items.name: 登特瀑布
items.subtitle: 默勒-鲁姆斯达尔郡
items.image_credit: World of Waterfalls (Johnny Cheng) / All Rights Reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Døntefossen (total height 745 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD from 1-m contour maps: 745 m in three sections; Wikipedia list and Norwegian Wikipedia ~700 m (−6%). Lakes above keep a fairly steady flow most of the year (frozen in winter); no flow-months figure, no badge.
items.image_hint: Døntefossen, Romsdalen valley between Flatmark and Verma, Rauma, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: a tall white fall in three sections (slabs, horsetail, final plunge) down the valley wall, seen from the E136 road across the Rauma river. NOT Vermafossen, NOT Mongefossen (dry), NOT Ølmåfossen.

items.name: 约塞米蒂瀑布
items.subtitle: 约塞米蒂国家公园

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Yosemite Falls (total height 739 m)

cross_check.name: USGS: highest measured waterfall in North America, 2,425 ft (739 m)

items.notes: 2,425 ft from François Matthes' 1913 USGS survey; WWD confirms with 1-m USGS lidar. Usually stops flowing in late summer/fall (WWD flow consistency 8 months).
items.image_hint: Yosemite Falls (Upper + Lower Yosemite Fall together), Yosemite Valley, Yosemite National Park, California, USA: the classic full view of both falls pouring off the granite wall in spring high flow, from Cook's Meadow / Swinging Bridge / the Merced River. NOT Bridalveil Fall, NOT Vernal or Nevada Fall, NOT Horsetail Fall (El Capitan), NOT lower-fall-only close-ups.

items.name: 云冠瀑布
items.subtitle: 华盛顿州

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Cloudcap Falls (total height 732 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: ~2,400 ft of continuous bedrock cascades, almost all hidden in an incised channel; flows only during the melt season. Wikipedia calls it more seasonal than Seahpo Peak Falls.
items.image_hint: Cloudcap Falls, below Cloudcap Peak / Jagged Ridge on the east shoulder of Mount Shuksan, Sulphide Creek basin, North Cascades National Park, Washington, USA: a long white cascade down dark glaciated rock among glaciers; aerial view. NOT Seahpo Peak Falls, NOT Sulphide Creek Falls, NOT Mount Shuksan from Picture Lake.

items.name: 博尔德冰川瀑布
items.subtitle: 冰川国家公园

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Boulder Glacier Falls (total height 727 m)

items.notes: WWD: ~2,350 ft chain of falls and cascades at the head of Bowman Creek's valley; glacier nearly gone, may become seasonal. No second source; no badge.
items.image_hint: Boulder Glacier Falls, headwall at the upper end of the Bowman Creek valley below Boulder Peak / Boulder Pass, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA: a long chain of white falls and cascades down a huge rock headwall; view from the Boulder Pass trail or Hole-in-the-Wall area. NOT Bowman Lake alone, NOT Grinnell Glacier falls.

items.name: 铁洞瀑布
items.subtitle: 留尼汪岛

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Trou de Fer (total height 725 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: initial horsetail ~213 m, then ~183 m, then ~305 m streams into the gorge and an ~24 m final plunge. Flows year-round (WWD 12 months). Réunion is an overseas region of France: flag = France.
items.image_hint: Trou de Fer, Réunion island (France, Indian Ocean): several white ribbon waterfalls plunging hundreds of metres into a deep, lush green volcanic gorge ('Iron Hole'); the classic helicopter view from above or the Bélouve forest viewpoint. NOT Cascade Niagara, NOT Langevin, NOT Voile de la Mariée (Salazie).

items.name: 谢拉格瀑布
items.subtitle: 吕瑟峡湾

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Kjeragfossen (total height 715 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: Single near-free-falling plunge, tallest free leap in Europe (WWD). Flows only with snowmelt or heavy rain; about 5 months a year (Wikipedia).
items.image_hint: Kjeragfossen, from the Kjerag plateau into the Lysefjord, Sandnes, Rogaland, Norway: one long free-falling white plume dropping off a sheer granite cliff straight to the fjord; spring snowmelt; view from a Lysefjord boat / ferry to Lysebotn. NOT Kjeragbolten boulder, NOT Preikestolen.

items.name: 尤塔赫瀑布
items.subtitle: 亚马孙州

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Yutajé (total height 715 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: surveyed 715 m (survey source not named), satellite relief consistent. Wikipedia list 'Salto Yutaj' 671 m (−6.2%). Flows year-round (WWD).
items.image_hint: Salto Yutajé (Yutajé Falls), Cerro Yutajé tepui, Manapiare, Amazonas state, Venezuela: a tall white plunge off the flat-topped tepui into a deep jungle gorge; aerial or lodge-area view. NOT Angel Falls, NOT Salto Pará.

items.name: 托格瀑布
items.subtitle: 默勒-鲁姆斯达尔郡
items.image_credit: World Waterfall Database / All rights reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Tågfossen (total height 710 m)

items.notes: WWD visited: one delicate horsetail of 710 m from a small lake; usually dry in late summer. Flow consistency 8 months. No second source.
items.image_hint: Tågfossen, Litldalen valley above lake Dalavatnet, Sunndal, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: a single long delicate white horsetail fall down very high sheer cliffs; view from the Litldalen road. NOT Vinnufossen or Skorga (Sunndalen).

items.name: 厄尔莫瀑布
items.subtitle: 鲁姆斯达尔山谷

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Ølmåfossen (total height 710 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: ~710 m veiling down the Trollveggen massif cliffs; Wikipedia list 720 m (+1.4%). Glacier and lakes; flow months not documented; no badge.
items.image_hint: Ølmåfossen, Romsdalen valley near Marstein, Rauma, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: a tall thin white fall veiling down the immense cliffs of the Trollveggen/Trolltindane massif, seen from the E136 / Marstein. NOT Mongefossen (dry, opposite side), NOT Trollveggen climbing shots without the waterfall.

items.name: 船童瀑布
items.subtitle: 西海岸大区

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Cabin Boy Falls (total height 701 m)

items.notes: WWD from 1:50,000 topo maps vs imagery: 700–750 m, possibly up to 800 m; listed at 701 m. Topo maps mark only a 124 m drop. No second source.
items.image_hint: Cabin Boy Falls, on the stream 'The Cabin Boy' below Cloudmaker Lake, Southern Alps, West Coast region, New Zealand (Mount Aspiring area): a long white fall down a steep glaciated valley wall in remote alpine terrain; aerial view.

items.name: 斯普雷讷瀑布
items.subtitle: 韦斯特兰郡

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Sprænefossen (total height 700 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia list (as 'Balåifossen', old WWD estimate)

items.notes: Official name Sprænefossen (Norgeskart); formerly listed as Balåifossen 850 m — WWD's 2011 survey cut it to ~700 m (Wikipedia still shows 850, +21%). Low volume, may dry in late summer (WWD 7 months).
items.image_hint: Sprænefossen (formerly called Balåifossen), Osafjord near Ulvik, Hardanger, Vestland, Norway: a long chain of white falls skipping and veiling down the steep fjord wall onto an alluvial fan by the sea; early-summer snowmelt. NOT Vøringsfossen, NOT Skykkjedalsfossen, NOT Steinsdalsfossen.

items.name: 无名湖瀑布
items.subtitle: 奥塔哥大区

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Lake Unknown Falls (total height 680 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD: falls drop out of Lake Unknown in several leaps to the Dart River valley floor; NZ topo shows only the 150 m upper leap. Flow months not documented.
items.image_hint: Lake Unknown Falls, on the wall of the Dart River valley (Mount Aspiring National Park, near Glenorchy, Otago, New Zealand): a big white fall leaping down a forested valley wall from Lake Unknown, seen from Dart River jet-boat tours. NOT Earnslaw Burn falls, NOT Routeburn falls.

items.name: 库克南瀑布
items.subtitle: 大萨瓦纳

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Kukenaam (total height 674 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: 674 m quoted from a Venezuelan National Park document (via WWD). WWD flow consistency 7 months. Often wrongly called one of the five tallest falls.
items.image_hint: Kukenán Falls (Salto Kukenán / Cuquenán), Kukenán-tepui (Matawi-tepui) beside Roraima, Gran Sabana, Canaima National Park, Bolívar, Venezuela: a long white plunge off the vertical tepui wall, savanna in front; view from the Roraima trek. NOT Angel Falls, NOT Roraima's own falls.

items.name: 西亚波峰瀑布
items.subtitle: 北喀斯喀特山脉
items.image_credit: Northwest Waterfall Survey / All rights reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Seahpo Peak Falls (total height 671 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: Seahpo Peak Falls (about 2,200 ft / 670 m)

items.notes: WWD: about 2,200 ft in several narrow tiers; flows well in summer but only while snow melts; Wikipedia calls it intermittent → SEASONAL.
items.image_hint: Seahpo Peak Falls, east arm of Mount Shuksan above the Sulphide Creek basin, North Cascades National Park, Washington, USA: narrow braided white tiers streaming down dark glaciated cliffs; aerial or Sulphide basin view. NOT Cloudcap Falls, NOT Sulphide Creek Falls.

items.name: 硫化物溪瀑布
items.subtitle: 北喀斯喀特山脉
items.image_credit: Northwest Waterfall Survey / All rights reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Sulphide Creek Falls (total height 665 m)

items.notes: WWD: almost 2,200 ft below Sulphide Lake outlet, mostly hidden in a narrow flume; year-round (WWD 12 months). Wikipedia article gives similar height (number not retrieved, API rate limit).
items.image_hint: Sulphide Creek Falls, from Sulphide Lake on the southeast side of Mount Shuksan, North Cascades National Park, Washington, USA: a powerful white fall in a narrow twisting gorge then tall tiers to a broad basin, seen straight-on from across the basin or from the air. NOT Seahpo Peak Falls, NOT Cloudcap Falls.

items.name: 埃格滕巴赫瀑布
items.subtitle: 劳特布龙嫩

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Äegertenbachfall (total height 660 m)

items.notes: WWD from topographic models: two tiers of ~230 m and ~330 m. No second source; flow months not documented.
items.image_hint: Ägertenbach falls (Äegertenbachfall / Ägertenbachfall), Lauterbrunnen Valley between Lauterbrunnen and Stechelberg, Bernese Oberland, Switzerland: a tall two-tier white waterfall down the sheer limestone valley wall above green meadows. NOT Staubbach Falls, NOT Mürrenbach Falls, NOT Trümmelbach Falls.

items.name: 马尔达尔斯瀑布
items.subtitle: 艾克斯达伦

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Mardalsfossen (total height 645 m)

cross_check.name: Statistics Norway (SSB) via WWD — head of the hydro scheme, 704 m

items.notes: Diverted into the Grytten hydro plant since 1977; licence guarantees a minimum release 20 June–20 August. WWD 645 m from topography; SSB 704 m reflects hydro head (+9%); often cited 655–705 m. WWD tallest drop 328 m (lower tier); upper free fall 262 m (often quoted 297 m).
items.image_hint: Mardalsfossen, Eikesdalen, Molde, Møre og Romsdal, Norway: a powerful white waterfall in two big plunges (upper free fall into a gorge) down a cliff above green birch forest, summer (June 20–August 20) when it flows; view from the Mardalsfossen trail. NOT Mongefossen.

items.name: 白瀑布
items.subtitle: 留尼汪岛

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Blanche (total height 640 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of waterfalls by height (rev 1379783845)

items.notes: WWD from French topo maps: from the ~840 m to ~200 m contour, four leaps, top drop ~400 m; some sources say up to 800 m. Best in the wet season; flow months not documented.
items.image_hint: Cascade Blanche (Cascade de la Ravine Blanche), on the wall of the Bras de Caverne canyon near Trou de Fer, Réunion island (France): a tall white four-step waterfall contrasting with the deep green jungle cliff; helicopter view. NOT Trou de Fer's main falls, NOT Voile de la Mariée.

items.name: 哨兵瀑布
items.subtitle: 约塞米蒂国家公园
items.image_credit: World Waterfall Database / All rights reserved

source.name: World Waterfall Database: Sentinel Fall (total height 631 m)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: Sentinel Falls (1,920 ft / 590 m)

items.notes: WWD (visited 2013): 2,070 ft in ~11 steps; Wikipedia 1,920 ft (−6.5%). Usually dries out by July (WWD flow consistency 6 months).
items.image_hint: Sentinel Fall, south wall of Yosemite Valley beside Sentinel Rock, Yosemite National Park, California, USA: a long series of white cascades down the granite wall next to Sentinel Rock in spring; view from Leidig Meadow / the valley floor. NOT Yosemite Falls (north wall), NOT Bridalveil Fall, NOT Staircase Falls.

insights.text: 季节性瀑布只在一年中的部分时段有水，水源是融雪或雨季径流。
津巴布韦穆塔拉齐瀑布常标762米，世界瀑布数据库估计约479米。
挪威蒙格瀑布高773米，本可上榜，却因水电开发自1977年起断流。
接下来这座瑞士瀑布，2020年经溪降者绳降测量，“长高”了90米。
安赫尔979米含807米主瀑下方急流；不算急流，948米的图盖拉更高。

scope_note: 统计口径：天然瀑布按总落差排名，从最高一级顶端量至最低一级底部，包含各级之间的跌水。高度原则上采用世界瀑布数据库数据；如有已公布的测量结果或纪录，则优先采用（安赫尔瀑布：吉尼斯世界纪录及1949年测量；图盖拉瀑布：吉尼斯世界纪录；云比拉瀑布：秘鲁国家地理研究所2007年测量）。收录对象为有名称、经该数据库实地测量或确认且注明依据的瀑布，以及有独立测量结果的瀑布。不收录未经核实的估测数据（如夏威夷的奥洛乌佩纳瀑布），也不收录因水电开发而断流的瀑布（如蒙格瀑布）。“季节性”表示每年仅部分时段有水。

layout.image_prefer: the WHOLE waterfall visible from top to bottom (or as much of it as possible), the right named waterfall (check the location), strong flow, the classic recognisable viewpoint, portrait orientation preferred
